claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that many informative filters do not match known motifs.

claims.claim: 373 recurrent annotated binding motifs with <5% FDR sequence similarity to the filters of the first CNN layer were identified.
claims.source: In total, we identified 373 recurrent annotated binding motifs with <5% false-discovery rate (FDR) sequence similarity to the filters of the first CNN layer, which were detected in >50 networks (Supplementary file 1-STable 3).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from motif analysis.

claims.claim: CNNs discovered binding motifs for all transcription factors included in the ChIP-seq training datasets.
claims.source: As expected, among the consistently-detected transcription factor motifs, we found motifs for all the transcription factors included in the ChIP-seq training datasets (CTCF, FOXA2, PDX1, MAFB, NKX2.2, NKX6.1).
claims.evidence: This is a result from motif analysis that validates the CNN approach.

claims.claim: CNNs discovered binding motifs for RFX6, HNF1A and NEUROD1 ab initio.
claims.source: Additionally, CNNs discovered, ab initio, binding motifs for several TFs that are known to be important for pancreatic development and for the maintenance of beta and alpha cell functions, including RFX6, HNF1A and NEUROD1 (Jennings et al., 2015; van der Meulen and Huising, 2015).
claims.evidence: This is a result from motif analysis supported by citations about the importance of these TFs.

claims.claim: RFX6, HNF1A and NEUROD1 are known to be important for pancreatic development and for the maintenance of beta and alpha cell functions.
claims.source: Additionally, CNNs discovered, ab initio, binding motifs for several TFs that are known to be important for pancreatic development and for the maintenance of beta and alpha cell functions, including RFX6, HNF1A and NEUROD1 (Jennings et al., 2015; van der Meulen and Huising, 2015).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Jennings et al., 2015 and van der Meulen and Huising, 2015.

claims.claim: CNN models of the pancreatic islet epigenome are capable of discovering well-established islet TF motifs ab initio from genomic sequences.
claims.source: This demonstrates that the CNN models of the pancreatic islet epigenome are capable of discovering well-established islet TF motifs ab initio from genomic sequences.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the motif discovery results.

claims.claim: The study applied islet CNN models for prioritization of T2D-associated variants from a GWAS study by Mahajan et al., 2018.
claims.source: Here, we applied the islet CNN models for prioritization of T2D-associated variants from a recently published GWAS study (Mahajan et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This describes the application of the CNN models.

claims.claim: The Mahajan et al. 2018 study identified 403 T2D-risk signals and performed genetic fine-mapping for 380 of them.
claims.source: This study of ~900,000 cases and controls of European ancestry, identified 403 T2D-risk signals, and performed genetic fine-mapping for 380 of them.
claims.evidence: This is information from the cited GWAS study.

claims.claim: CNN predictions were run for all 109,779 variants included within the 99% credible variant sets.
claims.source: We ran CNN predictions for all 109,779 variants included within the 99% credible variant sets for these signals, averaging the regulatory predictions for each variant and feature across 1000 individual CNN models to increase robustness.
claims.evidence: This describes the methodology for applying CNN models to variants.

claims.claim: A total of 11,389 variants with q-value <0.05 for any of the 30 features were identified.
claims.source: We identified a total of 11,389 variants with a q-value <0.05 for any of the 30 features, approximately 10% of the total number of credible set variants.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from the variant prioritization analysis.

claims.claim: Approximately 10% of credible set variants were identified as regulatory variants.
claims.source: We identified a total of 11,389 variants with a q-value <0.05 for any of the 30 features, approximately 10% of the total number of credible set variants.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from the variant prioritization analysis.

claims.claim: Variants with q < 0.05 were significantly more likely to be evolutionarily conserved than credible set variants with q > 0.05.
claims.source: Variants with q < 0.05 were significantly more likely to be evolutionarily conserved than the credible set variants with overall q > 0.05, as assessed by one-sided Wilcoxon rank sum test of the GERP scores (Cooper et al., 2005) (p=7.3e-04).
claims.evidence: This is a statistical result from comparing GERP scores.

claims.claim: 91 of the 403 T2D GWAS signals overlapped an islet eQTL (defined as p<10e-08).
claims.source: In this analysis, 91 of the 403 T2D GWAS signals from the largest published meta-analysis (Mahajan et al., 2018) overlapped an islet eQTL (defined as p<10e-08): of these, we identified overlapping regulatory variants (as predicted by the CNN q < 0.05) at 73 (~80%).
claims.evidence: This is a result from comparing CNN predictions with eQTL data.

claims.claim: Of the 91 T2D signals overlapping an islet eQTL, overlapping regulatory variants were identified at 73 (~80%).
claims.source: In this analysis, 91 of the 403 T2D GWAS signals from the largest published meta-analysis (Mahajan et al., 2018) overlapped an islet eQTL (defined as p<10e-08): of these, we identified overlapping regulatory variants (as predicted by the CNN q < 0.05) at 73 (~80%).
claims.evidence: This is a result from comparing CNN predictions with eQTL data.

claims.claim: Variants predicted to affect promoter or enhancer activities in islets were preferentially enriched among the top pancreatic islet eQTL results.
claims.source: We considered the enrichments of variants predicted to affect the six different groups of chromatin features, and found that variants predicted to affect promoter or enhancer activities in islets were preferentially enriched among the top pancreatic islet eQTL results (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated through enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: 137 pancreatic islet chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) were identified among the credible set variants.
claims.source: We used ATAC-seq data from a previously-published dataset of 17 human pancreatic islets (Thurner et al., 2018) to identify 137 pancreatic islet chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) among the credible set variants, and found these to be significantly enriched among the variants with the lowest CNN q-scores (p=6.9e-20).
claims.evidence: This is a result from analyzing ATAC-seq data.

claims.claim: caQTLs were significantly enriched among variants with the lowest CNN q-scores (p=6.9e-20).
claims.source: We used ATAC-seq data from a previously-published dataset of 17 human pancreatic islets (Thurner et al., 2018) to identify 137 pancreatic islet chromatin accessibility QTLs (caQTLs) among the credible set variants, and found these to be significantly enriched among the variants with the lowest CNN q-scores (p=6.9e-20).
claims.evidence: This is a statistical result from enrichment analysis.

claims.claim: Good agreement was observed between predicted disrupted regulatory elements and the variant location within them.
claims.source: Overall, we observed good agreement between the predicted disrupted regulatory elements and the variant located within them.
claims.evidence: This is a result from comparing CNN predictions with chromatin state maps.

claims.claim: A depletion of regulatory variants was observed within heterochromatin and other low methylation sites.
claims.source: Additionally, we observed a depletion of regulatory variants within heterochromatin and other low methylation sites.
claims.evidence: This is a result from analyzing overlap with chromatin states.

claims.claim: Enrichment of islet regulatory variants was observed among variants with highest PPAs compared to permutation-based random distribution (p=0.001).
claims.source: We observed enrichment of islet regulatory variants (CNN q < 0.05) among variants with highest PPAs (Figure 3A), compared to the permutation-based random distribution of regulatory variants (p=0.001).
claims.evidence: This is a statistical result from permutation testing shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: 28.8% of variants with gPPAs >= 0.8 had predicted regulatory effects with q < 0.05.
claims.source: Overall, we found that 28.8% of variants with gPPAs > = 0.8 had predicted regulatory effects with q < 0.05.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from analyzing convergence between gPPA and CNN predictions.

claims.claim: Variants with high fPPAs were enriched for CNN-predicted regulatory effects (p=0.001).
claims.source: As with the gPPAs, we observed that variants with high fPPAs, obtained through incorporating enrichments in regulatory elements from human pancreatic islet chromatin state maps (Thurner et al., 2018), were enriched for CNN-predicted regulatory effects (p=0.001)(Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This is a statistical result from enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: 40.6% of variants with fPPAs >= 0.8 had predicted regulatory effects with q < 0.05.
claims.source: Overall, 40.6% of variants with fPPAs > = 0.8 had predicted regulatory effects with q < 0.05.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from analyzing convergence between fPPA and CNN predictions.

claims.claim: Higher proportions of predicted regulatory variants were observed at higher PPA ranks within fine-mapped loci.
claims.source: Again, we observed higher proportions of predicted regulatory variants at higher PPA ranks within fine-mapped loci, when compared to random distribution of regulatory variants.
claims.evidence: This is a result from rank-based analysis.

claims.claim: The enrichment of islet CNN-regulatory variants was more marked within the top ranks of insulin secretion signals.
claims.source: Indeed, we observed that the enrichment of islet CNN-regulatory variants was more marked within the top ranks of insulin secretion signals.
claims.evidence: This is a result from comparing enrichment across signal types.

claims.claim: T2D signals characterized by a primary defect in insulin action showed no enrichment over the permuted background.
claims.source: In contrast, T2D signals characterized by a primary defect in insulin action (which typically involve mechanisms in liver, fat and muscle) showed no enrichment over the permuted background (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is a result from comparing enrichment across signal types shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: At 327 out of 380 fine-mapped signals, there was at least one predicted regulatory variant (q < 0.05).
claims.source: Overall, we found that, at 327 out of the 380 fine-mapped signals from the most recent European T2D GWAS study (Mahajan et al., 2018), there was at least one predicted regulatory variant (defined as q < 0.05).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from applying CNN predictions to fine-mapped signals.

claims.claim: Among 74 signals fine-mapped to a single variant (with gPPA or fPPA >= 80%), 28 variants were predicted to be regulatory in pancreatic islets.
claims.source: Among the 74 signals previously fine-mapped to a single variant (with gPPA or fPPA > = 80%), we found 28 variants predicted to be regulatory in pancreatic islets (Supplementary file 1-STable 4), in line with the previously reported overall enrichment of T2D-association signals in the regulatory elements specific to islets (Parker et al., 2013; Pasquali et al., 2014; Thurner et al., 2018; Miguel-Escalada et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result supported by citations to prior enrichment studies.

claims.claim: rs10830963 at MNTR1B was previously shown to alter enhancer activities.
claims.source: These included two well-studied variants (rs10830963 at MNTR1B, rs7903146 at TCF7L2), both previously shown to alter enhancer activities (Gaulton et al., 2015; Gaulton et al., 2010): these served as positive controls for the application of CNNs to functional variant prioritization.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Gaulton et al., 2015.

claims.claim: rs7903146 at TCF7L2 was previously shown to alter enhancer activities.
claims.source: These included two well-studied variants (rs10830963 at MNTR1B, rs7903146 at TCF7L2), both previously shown to alter enhancer activities (Gaulton et al., 2015; Gaulton et al., 2010): these served as positive controls for the application of CNNs to functional variant prioritization.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Gaulton et al., 2010.

claims.claim: 93 signals featured at least two variants with fPPAs >= 20%.
claims.source: Among the credible sets of variants, we identified 93 signals featuring at least two variants with fPPAs > = 20%, indicating that, even after functional fine-mapping, there is no unambiguously causal single variant.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from analyzing fine-mapping resolution.

claims.claim: At 37 of 93 signals with multiple high fPPA variants, CNNs predicted islet regulatory variants among the top fPPA candidates.
claims.source: At 37 of these 93 signals, CNNs predicted islet regulatory variants among the top fPPA candidates (Supplementary file 1-STable 5).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from applying CNN predictions.

claims.claim: At 25 signals, integration of CNN regulatory predictions highlighted a single most likely causal variant.
claims.source: At 25 signals, integration of CNN regulatory predictions downstream of the functional fine-mapping highlighted a single most likely causal variant, with either just a single islet regulatory variant predicted among the credible variants, or the top regulatory variant having much lower q-value (difference in -log10(q) > 100) than other predicted regulatory variants at the signal (a few such signals are highlighted in Figure 4 and Figure 5), narrowing down the list of candidates for further functional follow-up studies.
claims.evidence: This is a result from integrating CNN predictions with fine-mapping.

claims.claim: The PROX1 conditional signal has been fine-mapped to two plausible variants, rs79687284 and rs17712208.
claims.source: This conditional signal has been fine-mapped to two plausible variants, rs79687284 and rs17712208, on the basis of genetic and genomic data (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is a result from fine-mapping analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: rs79687284 and rs17712208 are in perfect LD (R2 = 1.0, D'=1.0).
claims.source: These variants are in perfect LD (R2 = 1.0, D'=1.0) and are located 376 bp apart within the same open strong enhancer in islets.
claims.evidence: This is a result from LD analysis.

claims.claim: rs79687284 and rs17712208 are located 376 bp apart within the same open strong enhancer in islets.
claims.source: These variants are in perfect LD (R2 = 1.0, D'=1.0) and are located 376 bp apart within the same open strong enhancer in islets.
claims.evidence: This is a result from genomic annotation analysis.

claims.claim: Strong allelic imbalance was observed at rs17712208 (p=1.55e-06) in pancreatic islet ATAC-seq data.
claims.source: When we investigated pancreatic islet ATAC-seq data from four individuals heterozygous for these two variants (as confirmed by array genotype data), we observed strong allelic imbalance at both variants (rs17712208 p=1.55e-06; rs79687284 p=6.10e-05) (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is a statistical result from ATAC-seq allelic imbalance analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Strong allelic imbalance was observed at rs79687284 (p=6.10e-05) in pancreatic islet ATAC-seq data.
claims.source: When we investigated pancreatic islet ATAC-seq data from four individuals heterozygous for these two variants (as confirmed by array genotype data), we observed strong allelic imbalance at both variants (rs17712208 p=1.55e-06; rs79687284 p=6.10e-05) (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is a statistical result from ATAC-seq allelic imbalance analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: rs17712208 was assigned a q-value of 1.69e-160 by the CNN.
claims.source: At this signal, both variants were scored as potentially regulatory by CNNs with q < 0.05, but the q-value at rs17712208 was much lower (q = 1.69e-160) highlighting this variant as the more likely regulatory candidate in the islets.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from CNN prediction.

claims.claim: The T2D risk A-allele at rs17712208 was predicted to lead to a significant reduction in the H3K27ac mark (△H3K27ac = −0.12).
claims.source: This q-value corresponded to a prediction that the T2D risk A-allele would lead to a significant reduction in the H3K27ac mark (△H3K27ac = −0.12) (Figure 5C) indicative of an active regulatory element presence.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from CNN prediction shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: rs79687284 was assigned a q-value of 0.002 by the CNN.
claims.source: The second variant, rs79687284, was assigned a much less remarkable q-value (q = 0.002) and only predicted to affect promoter features, with the top predictions pointing to a mild reduction of H3K4me3 mark in alpha and beta cells (△a_H3K4me3 = −0.01, △b_H3K4me3 = −0.01).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative result from CNN prediction.

claims.claim: In silico saturated mutagenesis revealed that the reference T-allele at rs17712208 is a crucial nucleotide in the HNF1B binding motif.
claims.source: We performed an in silico saturated mutagenesis for the rs17712208 variant (Figure 5D) to identify the regulatory sequence motifs at this locus affected by the variant. We observed that the reference T-allele is a crucial nucleotide in the HNF1B binding motif (Figure 5E), and that introduction of an A-allele at this position disrupts this motif, leading to predicted loss of the H3K27ac mark.
claims.evidence: This is a result from in silico mutagenesis analysis shown in Figures 5D and 5E.

claims.claim: Introduction of an A-allele at rs17712208 disrupts the HNF1B binding motif.
claims.source: We observed that the reference T-allele is a crucial nucleotide in the HNF1B binding motif (Figure 5E), and that introduction of an A-allele at this position disrupts this motif, leading to predicted loss of the H3K27ac mark.
claims.evidence: This is a result from in silico mutagenesis analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: PROX1 and HNF1B are co-expressed during pancreatic development in an iPSC-derived model of beta cell differentiation.
claims.source: We note that both PROX1 and HNF1B are co-expressed during pancreatic development in a previously published iPSC-derived model of beta cell differentiation (Perez-Alcantara et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citation to Perez-Alcantara et al., 2018.

claims.claim: The A-allele at rs17712208 resulted in significant repression of enhancer activity (p=0.0001) in luciferase reporter assay.
claims.source: Using an in vitro reporter assay, we confirmed that the A-allele at rs17712208 resulted in significant repression of enhancer activity (p=0.0001), while no significant change was observed for the T2D-risk allele at rs79687284 (p=0.15)(Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental result from luciferase assay shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: No significant change in enhancer activity was observed for the T2D-risk allele at rs79687284 (p=0.15) in luciferase reporter assay.
claims.source: Using an in vitro reporter assay, we confirmed that the A-allele at rs17712208 resulted in significant repression of enhancer activity (p=0.0001), while no significant change was observed for the T2D-risk allele at rs79687284 (p=0.15)(Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: This is an experimental result from luciferase assay shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: A modest but highly significant correlation was observed between islet CNN predictions and DeepSEA multi-tissue scores (r = 0.227, p<2.2e-16).
claims.source: Overall, we observed a modest but highly significant correlation of predictions with both these regulatory prediction scores reported by DeepSEA (multi-tissue: r = 0.227, p<2.2e-16; PanIslets: r = 0.223, p<2.2e-16) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 - AB).
claims.evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: A modest but highly significant correlation was observed between islet CNN predictions and DeepSEA PanIslets scores (r = 0.223, p<2.2e-16).
claims.source: Overall, we observed a modest but highly significant correlation of predictions with both these regulatory prediction scores reported by DeepSEA (multi-tissue: r = 0.227, p<2.2e-16; PanIslets: r = 0.223, p<2.2e-16) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 - AB).
claims.evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Both DeepSEA multi-tissue and PanIslets models performed better within T2D signals acting through insulin action rather than insulin secretion.
claims.source: However, both the multi-tissue and PanIslets DeepSEA models performed better within the subset of T2D signals acting through insulin action rather than through insulin secretion signals, predicting higher proportions of regulatory variants at top ranks of credible sets for the former, contrary to our expectations for the PanIslets model (Figure 3—figure supplement 1 - D).

results.result: CNNs trained on 30 pancreatic islet epigenomic features achieved high predictive performance, with best results for promoters (AUROC=0.95, AUPRC=0.70), TF binding (AUROC=0.89, AUPRC=0.48), and DNA accessibility (AUROC=0.89, AUPRC=0.65). Lower performance was observed for enhancers (AUROC=0.77, AUPRC=0.24), active regions (AUROC=0.82, AUPRC=0.37), and repressed regions (AUROC=0.79, AUPRC=0.20).
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C43 provide comprehensive quantitative performance metrics (AUROC and AUPRC) for all feature categories, with appropriate test set validation on held-out chromosome 2 data. The performance differences across features are clearly documented and supported by figures.

results.result: CNN convolutional filters captured regulatory sequence motifs, identifying 373 recurrent TF binding motifs including all TFs in training data (CTCF, FOXA2, PDX1, MAFB, NKX2.2, NKX6.1) and discovering ab initio motifs for islet-relevant TFs (RFX6, HNF1A, NEUROD1). Only 29/320 filters matched known motifs while 177 were informative, suggesting discovery of novel motifs.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C54 demonstrate successful motif discovery with quantitative results (373 motifs at <5% FDR, 29 annotated vs 177 informative filters). The recovery of expected TFs validates the approach, while ab initio discovery of known islet TFs (with supporting citations C53) provides biological validation.

results.result: Application of CNN models to 109,779 variants from 380 T2D fine-mapped signals identified 11,389 regulatory variants (q<0.05, ~10% of credible set). These variants showed significantly higher evolutionary conservation (GERP scores, p=7.3e-04) than non-regulatory variants.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C60 describe the application methodology and provide clear quantitative results with appropriate statistical testing. The evolutionary conservation analysis (C60) provides independent validation of regulatory predictions using established conservation metrics.

results.result: CNN-predicted regulatory variants showed enrichment in pancreatic islet eQTLs (73/91 signals, ~80%) and chromatin accessibility QTLs (137 caQTLs, p=6.9e-20). Variants predicted to affect promoter/enhancer activities were preferentially enriched among top eQTL results.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C65 provide multiple independent validations of CNN predictions using functional genomics data (eQTLs and caQTLs) with appropriate statistical testing. The enrichment analyses demonstrate biological relevance of predictions.

results.result: CNN-predicted regulatory variants showed good agreement with chromatin state annotations, with variants predicted to disrupt specific regulatory elements residing within those elements. Depletion was observed in heterochromatin and low methylation sites.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C67 demonstrate concordance between CNN predictions and independent chromatin state data, providing validation of prediction specificity. The depletion in heterochromatin is biologically expected and supports model validity.

results.result: CNN regulatory predictions converged with genetic and functional fine-mapping: regulatory variants were enriched among high gPPA variants (p=0.001, 28.8% at gPPA≥0.8) and high fPPA variants (p=0.001, 40.6% at fPPA≥0.8). Higher proportions of regulatory variants were observed at higher PPA ranks.
results.evaluation: Claims C68-C72 demonstrate convergence between CNN predictions and fine-mapping using rigorous permutation testing (1000 permutations). The quantitative enrichment metrics and statistical significance support the integration of these complementary approaches.

results.result: Enrichment of CNN-predicted regulatory variants was more pronounced for T2D signals acting through insulin secretion mechanisms compared to insulin action signals, which showed no enrichment over background.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C74 demonstrate tissue-specificity of the islet-trained CNN model by showing differential performance on signals with different mechanisms of action. This is biologically expected and validates the tissue-specific approach.

results.result: CNN models identified regulatory variants at 327/380 fine-mapped signals. Among 74 signals fine-mapped to single variants (gPPA or fPPA≥80%), 28 were predicted regulatory, including validated positive controls rs10830963 (MTNR1B) and rs7903146 (TCF7L2).
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C78 provide quantitative coverage statistics and include important positive controls with literature support (C77-C78). The identification of known functional variants validates the CNN approach for variant prioritization.

results.result: Among 93 signals with multiple high fPPA variants (≥20%), CNN predictions identified regulatory variants at 37 signals. At 25 signals, CNN integration highlighted a single most likely causal variant, refining fine-mapping resolution.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C81 demonstrate the practical utility of CNN predictions for refining ambiguous fine-mapping results. The quantitative results show meaningful refinement at a substantial fraction of signals requiring additional resolution.

results.result: At the PROX1 locus, two variants in perfect LD (rs79687284 and rs17712208) were distinguished by CNN: rs17712208 showed much lower q-value (1.69e-160 vs 0.002), predicted H3K27ac reduction (Δ=-0.12), disrupted HNF1B motif, and showed significant enhancer repression in luciferase assay (p=0.0001), while rs79687284 showed no significant effect (p=0.15).
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C94 provide comprehensive experimental validation of CNN predictions at a challenging locus with perfect LD. The integration of computational predictions (C87-C91), mechanistic insights (C90-C91), and experimental validation (C93-C94) strongly supports the causal role of rs17712208.

results.result: Comparison with DeepSEA showed modest correlation (r=0.227-0.223, p<2.2e-16) but islet CNN outperformed on insulin secretion signals. DeepSEA failed to identify known functional variants at MTNR1B and TCF7L2, and showed only borderline significance for PROX1 rs17712208 (PanIslets p=0.049). Tissue-specific motifs (NEUROD1, HNF1B) were better captured by islet CNN.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C106 provide systematic comparison with an established multi-tissue method, demonstrating advantages of tissue-specific training. The failure of DeepSEA on validated variants (C98-C99) and tissue-specific TFs (C102-C103) supports the value of tissue-specific models (C106).

results.result: CNNs successfully learned regulatory code from genomic sequences, with performance varying by feature type. Promoters, DNA accessibility, and TF binding were easiest to predict due to distinct sequence motifs. Performance was affected by data quality and number of training peaks.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C111 provide reasonable interpretation of performance differences based on established deep learning principles (C109) and biological characteristics of features (C111). The explanations are consistent with observed results and general knowledge.

results.result: The study observed convergence of genetic fine-mapping, functional fine-mapping, and CNN regulatory predictions, representing the first report of enrichment of in silico regulatory predictions among fine-mapped variants.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C113 summarize the key finding of convergence across methods. While C113's novelty claim cannot be fully verified without comprehensive literature review, the convergence itself is well-supported by multiple analyses (C68-C72).

results.result: CNN-prioritized variants were enriched in islet caQTLs and functional regulatory elements (promoters, strong open enhancers), consistent with prior studies. Integration with fine-mapping provides a powerful approach for identifying causal variants.
results.evaluation: Claims C115-C117 provide additional validation through concordance with prior functional genomics studies (with appropriate citations). The conclusion about integration with fine-mapping (C117) is supported by the comprehensive analyses presented.

results.result: GWAS have identified >400 T2D-associated signals, but identifying causal variants remains challenging as most map to non-coding sequences and likely act through transcriptional regulation.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C2, C6-C8 establish the research context with well-supported background information. C6 is supported by citation to Mahajan et al. 2018, while C7-C8 reflect established knowledge about GWAS findings.

results.result: Disease-associated variants likely perturb genes in disease-relevant tissues. T2D variants show enrichment in pancreatic islet enhancers, particularly in open chromatin/hypomethylated regions and 3D enhancer hubs. Islets are key for glucose homeostasis.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C13 provide well-cited background on tissue-specificity and islet biology. All claims are supported by appropriate citations to prior work (Marbach 2016, Battle 2017, Parker 2013, Pasquali 2014, Thurner 2018, Miguel-Escalada 2018).

results.result: Multiple epigenomic datasets exist for pancreatic islets and have been used for variant prioritization, but higher resolution methods are needed when multiple variants in LD reside in the same regulatory region. MPRAs offer a solution but are expensive and may not recapitulate cellular context.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C19 establish the methodological context with appropriate citations. The limitations of current approaches (C16) and MPRAs (C18-C19) are well-established in the field and properly cited.

results.result: CNNs are emerging tools for studying regulatory motifs and have been used for variant prioritization based on chromatin accessibility, modifications, and gene expression. Existing multi-tissue methods may miss tissue-specific regulatory grammar.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C23 are well-supported by citations to prior CNN work (Zhou & Troyanskaya 2015, Kelley 2016, Zhou 2018, Kelley 2018). C24 is speculative but represents a reasonable hypothesis motivating the tissue-specific approach.

results.result: The study trained tissue-specific CNNs on pancreatic islet epigenomic profiles to predict regulatory effects of T2D variants. The models recapitulate islet-specific regulatory grammar and can be integrated with fine-mapping for single-base resolution.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C27 accurately summarize the study's approach and main findings. C26 is supported by motif analysis results (C44-C54), while C27 is demonstrated through the PROX1 example (C82-C94).

results.result: Deep learning models can predict epigenome features from DNA sequence. CNN models trained on islet data show convergence with conventional variant prioritization and can refine T2D association signals with experimental validation.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C5 summarize the abstract's main findings. C3 is supported by prior work and methodology, C4 by convergence analyses (C68-C72), and C5 by the PROX1 validation (C82-C94).

results.result: A limitation is that tissue-specific CNN value depends on knowing the effector tissue. T2D involves multiple tissues (islets, liver, adipose, muscle), and tissues contain heterogeneous cell populations. Future cell-type-specific datasets may enable more precise inference.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C121 provide appropriate discussion of limitations and future directions. C119-C120 reflect established knowledge about T2D complexity and tissue heterogeneity. C121 is reasonable speculation about future improvements.

results.result: High-throughput experimental methods (MPRAs, HiDRA) have limitations including biases, errors, and restricted scope. CNN models can complement these by learning regulatory grammar and extrapolating to unassayed variants. Deep learning fine-mapping may become routine in GWAS analysis.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C123 accurately describe limitations of experimental methods with appropriate citations. C124-C125 are reasonable speculation about complementary roles and future adoption, consistent with the demonstrated utility of the approach.

results.result: A recent study (Liu et al. 2019) argued computational methods are not mature enough for GWAS fine-mapping, contrasting with the current findings.
results.evaluation: Claim C114 accurately cites a contrasting view from Liu et al. 2019. The current study's results provide evidence against this position through demonstrated convergence with fine-mapping and experimental validation.

results.result: Multi-tissue CNN models may be biased toward features present across all tissues and may not detect tissue-specific signals with high confidence.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C105 represent reasonable speculation about multi-tissue model limitations, supported by the comparative analysis with DeepSEA (C95-C103) showing better performance of tissue-specific models on tissue-specific signals.
